text: Bitcoin has clawed back most of its post-Fed dip, trading a shade above $77,000 and up around 1.5% on the day after briefly slipping under $76,000 earlier this week. That drop followed the Federal Reserve's quarter-point hike to 3.75-4.00%, its first increase in three years, which spooked institutions enough to pull nearly $750 million out of spot Bitcoin ETFs over two sessions, led by BlackRock's IBIT and Fidelity's FBTC. The bleeding continued into midweek, with another $296 million leaving Bitcoin funds and Ethereum ETFs shedding over $200 million of their own, so the big money is clearly still digesting the rate decision rather than piling back in. On-the-ground sentiment has swung back toward greed even as that ETF cash heads for the exits, and that kind of mismatch between price mood and real fund flows tends to precede a sharp move rather than calm. With institutional demand still shaky and the bounce happening on thinner volume, expect more choppy back-and-forth over the next few days rather than a clean trend. A real breakout only looks likely once ETF flows actually turn positive again, so the next couple of daily prints are worth watching closely.
